title: Special coordinate and coordinate vector are jointly uniform and independent
statement: Fix an integer $n \ge 1$, and consider the hard distribution on samples conditioned on the event that the generated input pair $(X,Y)$ is disjoint. Under this conditional law, the pair consisting of the special coordinate $T \in \{1,\dots,n\}$ and the generated disjoint coordinate vector $c \colon \{1,\dots,n\} \to \{\text{neither}, \text{leftOnly}, \text{rightOnly}\}$ has the same distribution as a pair of independent random variables in which $T$ is uniform on $\{1,\dots,n\}$ and $c$ is uniform on all $3^{n}$ coordinate vectors. In particular $T$ and $c$ are independent, and each is uniformly distributed on its range.
hypotheses_covered: n is a positive natural number
law is the hard distribution conditioned on the disjointness event D
comparison measure is the product of the uniform law on the special coordinate and the uniform law on disjoint coordinate vectors
replaced: Under $D$, the special coordinate and generated disjoint coordinate vector have the product law: $T$ is uniform and independent of the disjoint coordinate vector.
